heading: INT. FOG-SIGNAL STATION - LIGHTHOUSE BASE - NIGHT

units.text: INT. FOG-SIGNAL STATION - LIGHTHOUSE BASE - NIGHT
A round stone room the size of a chapel, its walls sweating.
A brass foghorn compressor squats in the center like a sleeping animal.
Oil lamps gutter on iron hooks.
Everything smells of kelp and rust.
ORVILLE HASKELL (60s, gaunt, a keeper's wool coat gone green at the seams) kneels before the compressor with a wrench, his breath smoking.
MRS. DELPHINE VOSS (50s, widow's black, pearl buttons, a face carved from candle wax) stands in the doorway holding a covered birdcage.
You shouldn't have rowed out in this.
units.name: HASKELL

units.text: Neither should you have stayed.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: She sets the cage on a crate.
Something inside shifts and settles.
It stopped knocking an hour ago.
units.name: HASKELL

units.text: Then it has what it wanted.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: A shortwave radio on the shelf crackles.
Haskell flinches, then crosses to it.
Station Nine, this is Coast Guard Relay. Do you read? Over.
units.name: TAMSIN

units.text: Haskell thumbs the key.
Relay, Station Nine. Fog is lifting. All quiet here.
units.name: HASKELL

units.text: Copy, quiet. Your lamp is out, Mr. Haskell. We show no light from the tower.
units.name: TAMSIN

units.text: Haskell looks up the spiral stair.
Black.
Delphine lifts the cloth from the birdcage.
Empty.
The little door hangs open.
Tell her we'll light it at dawn.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: At dawn, Relay. Station Nine out.
units.name: HASKELL

units.text: He clicks the radio off.
Far above them, slow and deliberate, something descends one step at a time.
Gentle now. He is only tired.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: Haskell sits on the crate, the wrench loose in his hand, and watches the stair with the patience of a man who has run out of fear.
